speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To better understand your condition, can you describe the appearance of the rash on your palms and when the symptoms typically worsen?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of an itchy rash on his upper body and face. Additionally, he has been experiencing a numbness and tingling sensation on both palms. He has been working on his family's rice farm, also caring for livestock.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Do you notice if the rash becomes more prominent or itchy when you are exposed to sunlight, and have you experienced any hair thinning or loss during this year?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pruritic rash on upper body and face. I also have Numbness and tingling sensation of both palms, Thinning of the eyebrows, Loss of some eyelashes, Hypopigmented macules around the elbows.

speaker: Doctor
text: You have mentioned thinning eyebrows, loss of eyelashes, and hypopigmented macules around your elbows. Have you noticed any darkening or hyperpigmentation of your skin in areas exposed to the sun, and do you have any difficulty swallowing?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Social history: Works as a farmer, no history of travel outside the local area.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any joint pain or swelling, and have you noticed any tightening of the skin on your fingers or hands?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, weight loss, changes in vision, or any respiratory symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of a pruritic rash on sun-exposed areas, hair loss (eyebrows/eyelashes), and paresthesias is highly suggestive of Pellagra, especially given your occupation as a rice farmer which may indicate a diet lacking in niacin. To confirm this, I need to check your nutritional status and rule out other causes. REQUEST TEST: Serum_Niacin_Level

speaker: Doctor
text: Normal serum niacin levels make Pellagra unlikely, so I need to consider other causes for the hair loss, rash, and paresthesias. Do you have any history of tick bites, and have you noticed a "bull's-eye" rash at any point?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, weight loss, changes in vision, or any respiratory symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the combination of pruritic rash on sun-exposed areas, alopecia (eyebrows/eyelashes), and paresthesias, along with your occupation, this clinical picture is classic for Pellagra (Niacin/B3 deficiency), despite the potentially misleading serum test. I will request specific antibody tests to definitively rule out autoimmune causes like Lupus or Dermatomyositis. REQUEST TEST: ANA_and_Anti-Smith_Antibodies

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal ANA and Anti-Smith antibodies effectively rule out Systemic Lupus Erythematosus and Dermatomyositis. Given the classic triad of dermatitis (photosensitive rash, Casal necklace equivalent), alopecia, and neuropathy (paresthesias), along with the risk factor of a rice-heavy diet, the clinical diagnosis is Pellagra. DIAGNOSIS READY: Pellagra
